description: The runtime save: the save document a running game writes its state into and loads it from (PL.core-load-refused-message, PL.core-load-refusal-codes; rulings U118(5), U124(1), U49(3)). New Game makes it the fresh document the host builds for a new game, whatever was loaded or saved before, so a New Game after a Load starts from a fresh runtime save and its first save carries nothing of the loaded one. A Load first refuses a save that is not the game's own, another world's (wrong_world) and then another runtime's (wrong_runtime, C5-3), then whatever the checked read refuses; one it accepts replaces the runtime save. A refused Load changes nothing and shows core's invalid_format message (SLOT_MESSAGES.invalid_format) for every refusal code. A Save writes into it with the checked writer; a refused Save changes nothing. Runner: src/runtime-save-corpus.ts (op run; steps new_game, load, save). Numbers compare within tolerance; everything else exactly, object key sets included. Regenerate with npm run runtime-save-corpus; npm run runtime-save-corpus:check fails on any difference.
sources: Rules new in core (src/runtime-save.ts), stated for Unreal's run 14 p8 m1-m3 (requests/to-manager/2026-11-16-unreal-run14 item 5): New Game after a Load (reachable under -InsimulNoOnboarding) and the pause menu's Load refused for unreadable_*.

The ownership codes wrong_world and wrong_runtime (PL.core-load-refusal-codes, U124(1)) state what Unreal's DescribeSlot answered not_this_game for: SaveWorldIsSession (another world's save) and ReadRuntimeSave's C5-3 check (Portable/InsimulVillageSave.cpp, saveBelongsTo), in that order.

Save documents and game states are synthetic, in the village-state corpus's shapes (scripts/emit-village-state-corpus.ts); every expected is core's answer, and src/conformance/__tests__/runtime-save.test.ts pins the same rules independently.

contract.newGameRule: new_game: the runtime save becomes a copy of the fresh document (input.fresh), whatever was loaded or saved before; it is never the loaded document
contract.loadRule: load: readRuntimeSave(document, readOptions.worldId, readOptions.runtime, absent meaning null, the legacy runtime): ownershipRule, then readVillageSave(document, readOptions); accepted, the document becomes the runtime save; refused, the runtime save is unchanged and the result is {ok: false, refusal: {code, field}, outcome, message}
contract.ownershipRule: before the checked read, in this order: document.worldId (absent: none) must be readOptions.worldId, else wrong_world (field worldId); the runtime stamp on the player agent's board (saveRuntimeOf; none: null) must be readOptions.runtime (absent: null), else wrong_runtime (field runtime, the C5-3 rule, saveBelongsTo)
contract.refusedLoadRule: every refusal code (the codes core states, loadRefusalOutcomes, and any other string: unstatedRefusalOutcome) is the slot outcome invalid_format, and the message is refusedLoadMessage (SLOT_MESSAGES.invalid_format); an engine shows that message and no words of its own
contract.saveRule: save: writeVillageSave(runtimeSave, gameState, writeOptions); accepted, the runtime save becomes {...runtimeSave, currentState, conversations} as written; refused, it is unchanged and the result is {ok: false, refusal: {code, field}}
contract.freshRule: fresh: the runtime save equals input.fresh as canonical JSON (keys sorted at every depth)
contract.refusedLoadMessage: Unrecognized save format — this slot cannot be loaded.

cases.name: the runtime save starts as the fresh document
New Game at the start keeps the fresh document
Load, then New Game: the runtime save is the fresh document again, not the loaded one
cases.note: U118(5): New Game after a Load starts from a fresh runtime save. After the Load the runtime save is the loaded document (fresh false); New Game makes it the fresh document (fresh true).

cases.name: Load, then New Game, then Save: the new game's first save carries nothing of the loaded one
cases.note: The written save equals the one in "New Game at the start, then Save" (a test pins the two equal): no stored conversation row, Prolog fact, dynamic quest, quest progress or storm of the loaded save rides into it.

cases.name: New Game at the start, then Save: the fresh document with the new game's state
cases.note: The control for the case above.

cases.name: Load, then Save, with no New Game: the save writes into the loaded document
cases.note: The control that shows the New Game case can fail: without New Game the loaded save's stored rows, facts and dynamic quests ride into the write, so this runtime save differs from the New Game one.

cases.name: Save, then New Game: the game's own save is not carried either
Load, Load again, then New Game: the fresh document, whichever save was loaded last
a Load refused wrong_version shows core's invalid_format message and leaves the runtime save as it was
cases.note: The second save has a SaveFile version this core does not know. U118(5), U124(1), U49(3): every refusal of a Load (the ownership codes and the checked read's) is the slot outcome invalid_format with SLOT_MESSAGES.invalid_format, never an engine's own words; the runtime save stays the loaded game's (fresh false).
